newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jews protest at Hebron pullout work.
newsitem.headline: Jews protest at Hebron pullout work.

text.p: Jewish settlers tore down a steel platform and stairs before Israeli soldiers could finish building a room to be used for Israeli-PLO coordination after Israel pulls out of Hebron, witnesses said on Monday.

They said some 50 Jewish settlers were protesting at the building of the room on al-Shuhada (martyrs) road linking two Jewish enclaves in Hebron's old city. They cursed passing Arabs and read from holy writings.
Witnesses said Israeli security forces did not try to stop the settlers but afterwards picked up the platform and stairs and put them away.
The Israeli army said it was checking the report.

The building of the room and the erecting of large cement blocks around police offices near the Tomb of the Patriarchs, also known as al-Ibrahimi mosque, were the first signs of preparations for a partial Israeli troop pullout from Hebron.

PLO security official in the Hebron area, Brigadier-General Abdel-Fattah al-Jeidi, said the room would serve as a branch of the joint Israeli-PLO District Coordination Office (DCO) in the heart of Hebron after Israeli troops evacuate about 80 percent of the city.
"The building of this DCO branch is in line with the 1995 Hebron deal. It will only operate after an accord on mechanisms of implementing that deal is reached," he told Reuters.

After three weeks of intensive talks Israeli and PLO officials failed to reach agreement on implementing a Hebron deal signed between the PLO and Israel's previous government in September of last year.
Israel wants to boost security for the 400 Jewish settlers living and studying in the Arab city, while Palestinians reject attempts by Israel to renegotiate the signed deal.
